subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan for FinServCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan for FinServCorp

Hi Julia —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the demo. Really appreciate the openness on the architecture and the evaluation priorities. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the proposed POC approach so your team can review and confirm next steps. I’ve attached a short one-page POC outline for reference (Redwood_POC_Outline_2026-02-26.pdf).

TL;DR proposed POC (3 weeks):
- Success criteria (must-haves):
  - End-to-end inference latency <= 250ms p95 for your 1k QPS simulation (50-token avg).
  - Per-token cost at or below target threshold agreed during call (initial planning target $0.0009/token).
  - No data egress from your VPC; keys managed by your KMS during Private deployment (if chosen).
- Evaluation workstreams and owners:
  - Integration & infra (FinServ): Carlos + IT team — deploy test harness and traffic generator.
  - Model & performance (Redwood): Vivek — optimize batching, quantization profile.
  - Results & product fit (FinServ + Redwood): Julia + Marissa — weekly sync and final sign-off.
- Timeline (proposed):
  - Week 0 (kickoff): 1-hour alignment + environment access
  - Week 1: baseline run (no optimizations) and instrumentation
  - Week 2: performance tuning (batching, cache) + cost analysis
  - Week 3: final validation, review results, and decision meeting

Open questions to address during kickoff:
- Which environment do you prefer to run the POC in? Hosted Redwood API (fastest to stand up) or Private (VPC/on-prem) for final fidelity?
- Who should be the main SRE/engineer contact for environment access and firewall coordination?

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm kickoff window: we have availability the week of Mar 8.
2) Share test dataset and representative traffic profile by EOD Tue, Mar 2.
3) Email confirmation to proceed so we can schedule Vivek for tuning work.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once I hear back.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_POC_Outline_2026-02-26.pdf (1 page - POC objectives, timeline, ownership)

From: Julia Park <julia.park@finservcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finservcorp.com>, FinServCorp IT <it@finservcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan for FinServCorp

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few quick items from our side:

1) Environment: for the POC we prefer to start on Redwood's hosted infra to speed things up, then validate final runs in our VPC if results look promising.
2) Contacts: Carlos will be the technical lead (he’s CC'd) and I will own product sign-off. IT (it@finservcorp.com) will help with firewall/NAT setup.
3) Timeline: week of Mar 8 works for us; is Mar 9 or Mar 10 better for kickoff?

Clarifying questions:
- Is the per-token cost target adjustable after the baseline run? We want to see the delta pre/post optimizations.
- For latency, can we add a p50 target as a secondary metric?

If you can confirm kickoff details and share the Drive link for the POC outline, we’ll get the test dataset and traffic profile to you by Mar 2.

Thanks — Julia
Product Manager, FinServCorp
Julia.Park@finservcorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finservcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan for FinServCorp

Hi Julia — great, thanks for the quick responses.

Answers inline:
- Cost target: yes — the $0.0009/token is an initial planning target. We will measure baseline cost during Week 1 and iterate on optimizations in Week 2; we’ll produce a simple delta report so you can decide on acceptable thresholds.
- Latency: we can add p50 as a secondary metric; proposed targets: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms.

Kickoff: Mar 9 at 10:00am PT works for our team. I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Drive link for the POC outline: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B_PoCOutline (same doc as attached).

Next steps (summary):
- You (FinServ): share test dataset + traffic profile by Mar 2.
- We (Redwood): reserve time for Vivek Mar 9-20 for tuning, schedule weekly checkpoints.

I’ll loop Stephanie in on billing/credits or trial terms for the POC if needed.

Cheers,
Marissa

Hi all — thanks for confirming the kickoff. Quick technical notes ahead of Mar 9:

- For hosted evaluation, please provide a sample of your top 5 representative prompts and average token lengths. That helps me pick an initial batching profile.
- If you have any custom tokenization quirks (e.g., pre/post-processing), share a short snippet so latency measurements are realistic.
- I’ll bring a short checklist to the kickoff: dataset access, auth (API key vs. mTLS), traffic generator configuration, and a list of endpoints to hit for tracing.

I’ll reserve Mar 9-10 AMPT for the kickoff and have time slots blocked for tuning work the following week.

-Vivek
